issues.description: Endpoint path mismatch for Person CRUD operations: the problem statement and the client code (template & solution) expect endpoints under /persons (e.g. POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId}), but the server implementation in the solution repository exposes these endpoints under /people (e.g. @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people"), etc.). This discrepancy means a working client (or student implementing server per the problem) will not be able to communicate with the server as implemented in the solution, and students will be confused which path to use when implementing/testing their endpoints.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the server endpoint paths consistent with the problem statement and client code. Change the mappings in the server PersonResource from "people" to "persons" (e.g. @GetMapping("persons"), @PostMapping("persons"), @PutMapping("persons/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("persons/{personId}")). Alternatively, if "people" is preferred, update the problem statement and all client code to use "people". The recommended fix is to use /persons to match the exercise description and the client templates.

issues.description: The problem statement and the client-side controller refer to the persons endpoint as "/persons" (the specified endpoints are POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId}), but the server-side REST resource in the solution is implemented under the path "people" (e.g., @GetMapping("people"), @PostMapping("people"), etc.). This naming mismatch ("persons" vs. "people") refers to the same conceptual entity (person collection endpoints) but uses different identifiers across artifacts. As a result, students following the problem statement or implementing the client calls to /persons will be unable to map those requirements to the server implementation and their HTTP requests will not reach the server, creating significant confusion and wasted effort.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single consistent endpoint name across all artifacts. Align the server endpoints with the problem statement and client by renaming the server mappings from "people" to "persons" (change @GetMapping("people") -> @GetMapping("persons"), @PostMapping("people") -> @PostMapping("persons"), @PutMapping("people/{personId}") -> @PutMapping("persons/{personId}"), and @DeleteMapping("people/{personId}") -> @DeleteMapping("persons/{personId}")). Alternatively, if you prefer "people", update the problem statement and client controller URIs to use "/people". Preferably choose "persons" to match the explicit endpoints in the exercise description so students can directly map requirements to the code.
